it is non deterministic automata with λ transition

it is LIFO stack

pages.title: δ the transition function
pages.text:
δ the transition function

There are 4 transition that we can make
1. δ(p, a, A) = (q, λ) this mean we pop A from the stack
2. δ(p, a, A) = (q, A) we does not change any thing in the stack
3. δ(p, a, A) = (q, X) we replace A with X in the stack
4. δ(p, a, A) = (q, XY) we replace A with Y then add X to the stack

Configuration of PDA

represented by:
Triple (q, w, γ) called instantaneous description or ID
q is current state
w is remaining input
γ is the content of the stack from left to right
⊢ this notation describe the change
⊢* stack is from left to right

pages.title: Deterministic pushdown automata
pages.text:
Deterministic pushdown automata

DPDA is determined by 2 conditions:
- ∀ q ∈ Q for each state q ∈ Q
∀ a ∈ Σ ∪ {λ} for every character a ∈ alphabet
∀ X ∈ Γ for every X ∈ stack
the set δ(q, a, X) has at most one element
∀ q ∈ Q
∀ a ∈ Σ ∪ {λ}
∀ X ∈ Γ
the two sets δ(q, a, X) and δ(q, λ, X) cannot
both be non empty (at least one is empty)

pages.title: CFG Ex
pages.text:
CFG Ex

Find the language generated by the following CFG over alphabet: Σ = {a, b}
1) S -> aS | bS | λ
= (a + b)*
2) S -> SS | bS | a
= (b* a)*
3) S -> SaS | b
= (ba)* b
4) S -> aT | bT | λ ; T -> aS | bS
= word of even length

Find a CFG generation the following languages:

a) L = (ab)* a
S -> abS | a
b) L = (ab)* + (ba)*
S -> A | B ; A -> abA | λ ; B -> baB | λ
c) L = a* b (bb)*
S -> Abb ; A -> aA | λ ; B -> bbB | λ
d) L = a* b (b* a)*
S -> A | B
A -> aA | b
B -> aB | λ
C -> bC | λ

pages.title: Residual method
pages.text:
Residual method:

So we keep dividing until no new state appears and finaly we draw the states.

Palindrome : symmetric with respect to center

CFG Derivation:

Recursive inference :
a) S -> aX | bY | λ
X -> aS | bZ
Y -> bS | aZ
Z -> aY | bX
aababa ?
a ∈ Q0, S
Left most derivation:
S -> aX -> aaS -> aabY -> aabaZ -> aababa
right most derivation:
Same but start from right

Construct PDA

So first the stack is used as memory, so any time we need to remember some thing we use stack - we calculate all the transitions and what we should append to the stack and if we should move to another state.
